524	def scheme_frontier(capacity: Any, budgets: Any) -> tuple[Params, ...]:
525	    """Return every feasible, non-dominated scheme configuration as a tuple.
526	
527	    The non-dominated-frontier counterpart of :func:`recommend_scheme`:
528	    instead of ranking the feasible configs and returning one preference's
529	    winner, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
530	    inspect the trade-off between one-signature size and verifier chain
531	    steps. The candidate set is exactly the one :func:`recommend_scheme`
532	    documents — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS with ``w`` 4
533	    and 8) at ``capacity == 1`` and every Merkle configuration with ``w``
534	    in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 whose capacity covers the
535	    requested count — and the capacity, one-signature serialised-size
536	    (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and verifier hash-chain step
537	    (:attr:`Params.steps`) metrics are field-for-field the values
538	    :func:`profile` reports.
539	
540	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
541	    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
542	    signature's serialised size and on the verifier hash-chain step count.
543	    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
544	    integer, and at least one entry must be set; a candidate exceeding
545	    either bound is excluded. There is no preference parameter: no
546	    configuration trading chain steps for signature size (or the reverse)
547	    is discarded ahead of the dominance test, so both the speed and the
548	    size end of the trade-off survive.
549	
550	    A feasible candidate *A* dominates another feasible candidate *B*
551	    when ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on both costs — signature bytes
552	    and verifier steps — and strictly smaller on at least one. Every
553	    dominated candidate is dropped and the survivors are deduplicated by
554	    value. The returned tuple is sorted stably and ascending by verifier
555	    steps, signature bytes, spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the
556	    requested count), scheme name, ``w`` and ``height``; a missing
557	    parameter sorts ahead of any value at its position.
558	
559	    Validation reuses :func:`recommend_scheme`'s rules in its capacity-
560	    then-budgets order: a non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a
561	    boolean, non-integer or out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or
562	    otherwise illegal ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``)
563	    or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError`` — an
564	    empty tuple is never returned. The function is pure: it draws no
565	    randomness, generates no keys and changes no state, and repeated calls
566	    with the same inputs return item-for-item identical results.
567	    """
568	    capacity = _validate_scheme_capacity(capacity)
569	    signature_limit, steps_limit = _validate_scheme_budgets(budgets)
570	
571	    feasible: list[Params] = []
572	    for candidate in _scheme_candidates(capacity):
573	        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
574	            continue
575	        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
576	            continue
577	        feasible.append(candidate)
578	    if not feasible:
579	        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")
580	
581	    def dominates(a: Params, b: Params) -> bool:
582	        no_worse = a.sig_bytes <= b.sig_bytes and a.steps <= b.steps
583	        strictly_better = a.sig_bytes < b.sig_bytes or a.steps < b.steps
584	        return no_worse and strictly_better
585	
586	    non_dominated = [
587	        candidate
588	        for candidate in feasible
589	        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in feasible)
590	    ]
591	
592	    unique: list[Params] = []
593	    seen: set[Params] = set()
594	    for candidate in non_dominated:
595	        if candidate not in seen:
596	            seen.add(candidate)
597	            unique.append(candidate)
598	
599	    unique.sort(
600	        key=lambda candidate: (
601	            candidate.steps,
602	            candidate.sig_bytes,
603	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
604	            candidate.scheme,
605	            candidate.w is not None,
606	            candidate.w,
607	            candidate.height is not None,
608	            candidate.height,
609	        )
610	    )
611	    return tuple(unique)
612

614	def _validate_scheme_weights(weights: Any) -> tuple[int, int]:
615	    """Validate the two-tuple of non-negative scheme cost weights."""
616	    if not isinstance(weights, tuple):
617	        raise TypeError("weights must be a 2-tuple of non-negative integer weights")
618	    if len(weights) != 2:
619	        raise ValueError("weights must contain exactly two entries")
620	    for weight in weights:
621	        if isinstance(weight, bool):
622	            raise ValueError("every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
623	        if not isinstance(weight, int):
624	            raise TypeError("every weight must be an integer")
625	        if weight < 0:
626	            raise ValueError("every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
627	    if not any(weight > 0 for weight in weights):
628	        raise ValueError("at least one weight must be positive")
629	    return weights

632	def recommend_scheme_weighted(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, weights: Any) -> Params:
633	    """Pick one non-dominated scheme configuration by weighted normalised costs.
634	
635	    Computes :func:`scheme_frontier` exactly once and ranks the returned
636	    feasible, non-dominated cross-scheme configurations by a
637	    caller-supplied linear score over two costs: one signature's
638	    serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier
639	    hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`).
640	
641	    ``weights`` must be a two-tuple in that same order — single-signature
642	    serialised size and verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a
643	    non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least one must be positive.
644	    Each of the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier
645	    as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``; the
646	    weighted score is the sum of the two normalised costs times their
647	    weights, divided by the weight total, all compared as exact rationals
648	    (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point anywhere. The survivor
649	    with the smallest score is returned; equal scores use
650	    :func:`recommend_scheme`'s existing tie-break tail: spare capacity
651	    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), scheme name,
652	    then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing parameter sorted ahead of any
653	    value. The candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
654	    duplicated: the frontier is the only source of candidates and is
655	    called exactly once, so the returned :class:`Params` is field-for-field
656	    a member of the tuple one same-argument :func:`scheme_frontier` call
657	    returns.
658	
659	    ``capacity`` and ``budgets`` follow :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types,
660	    ranges, inclusive-budget, exception and no-feasible-candidate rules
661	    exactly, so a violation raises exactly as that function does (and is
662	    screened before ``weights``). A non-tuple ``weights`` or a
663	    non-integer member raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a
664	    boolean, negative or all-zero weight raises ``ValueError``. The
665	    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and
666	    changes no state.
667	    """
668	    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
669	    validated_weights = _validate_scheme_weights(weights)
670	
671	    metric_rows = tuple(
672	        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
673	    )
674	    spans = tuple(
675	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
676	        for i in range(2)
677	    )
678	    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)
679	
680	    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
681	        score = Fraction(0)
682	        for value, weight, (low, high) in zip(
683	            (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps), validated_weights, spans
684	        ):
685	            if high > low:
686	                score += weight * Fraction(value - low, high - low)
687	        score /= weight_total
688	        return (
689	            score,
690	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
691	            candidate.scheme,
692	            candidate.w is not None,
693	            candidate.w,
694	            candidate.height is not None,
695	            candidate.height,
696	        )
697	
698	    return min(frontier, key=ranking)
699

701	def _validate_scheme_weight_scenarios(
702	    scenarios: Any,
703	) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]:
704	    """Validate the non-empty tuple of two-weight scenarios."""
705	    if not isinstance(scenarios, tuple):
706	        raise TypeError("scenarios must be a tuple of two-tuples of weights")
707	    if not scenarios:
708	        raise ValueError("scenarios must not be empty")
709	    validated = []
710	    for scenario in scenarios:
711	        if not isinstance(scenario, tuple):
712	            raise TypeError("every scenario must be a two-tuple of weights")
713	        if len(scenario) != 2:
714	            raise ValueError("every scenario must contain exactly two entries")
715	        for weight in scenario:
716	            if isinstance(weight, bool):
717	                raise ValueError(
718	                    "every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer"
719	                )
720	            if not isinstance(weight, int):
721	                raise TypeError("every weight must be an integer")
722	            if weight < 0:
723	                raise ValueError(
724	                    "every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer"
725	                )
726	        if not any(weight > 0 for weight in scenario):
727	            raise ValueError(
728	                "every scenario must contain at least one positive weight"
729	            )
730	        validated.append(scenario)
731	    return tuple(validated)

734	def recommend_scheme_weighted_scenarios(
735	    capacity: Any,
736	    budgets: Any,
737	    scenarios: Any,
738	) -> Params:
739	    """Pick one non-dominated scheme minimising worst regret over scenarios.
740	
741	    The preference-drift-robust counterpart of
742	    :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted`: instead of trusting one fixed
743	    two-tuple of cost weights, it evaluates several weight scenarios at
744	    once and picks the member of :func:`scheme_frontier`'s returned
745	    feasible, non-dominated cross-scheme frontier with the smallest
746	    worst-case regret — the maximum, over scenarios, of how much worse
747	    the chosen configuration scores than the best configuration for that
748	    scenario. The two weighted costs, in order, are one signature's
749	    serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier
750	    hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`).
751	
752	    ``scenarios`` must be a non-empty tuple; each member must itself be a
753	    two-tuple in that same order — single-signature serialised size and
754	    verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a non-boolean,
755	    non-negative integer and at least one weight of each scenario must be
756	    positive; repeated scenarios are counted separately.
757	
758	    The frontier is computed exactly once and is the only source of
759	    candidates — the candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
760	    duplicated, no randomness is drawn and no keys are generated. Each of
761	    the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier as
762	    ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``. For each
763	    scenario, a candidate's score is the weighted sum of its two
764	    normalised costs divided by the scenario's weight total, all compared
765	    as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point
766	    anywhere. Each scenario's own minimum score is then subtracted from
767	    every candidate's score to give that scenario's regret; candidates
768	    are ranked first by the greatest regret over the scenarios (the
769	    minimax-regret choice), then by the sum of the regrets, then by the
770	    tuple of per-scenario scores, all ascending. Every ranking finishes
771	    with the same ascending tie-break as every other cross-scheme
772	    ranking — spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the requested
773	    signature count), scheme name, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a
774	    missing parameter sorted ahead of any value — and the first survivor
775	    is returned as a :class:`Params`, field-for-field a member of the
776	    tuple one same-argument :func:`scheme_frontier` call returns.
777	
778	    ``capacity`` and the two-tuple ``budgets`` follow
779	    :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget, exception
780	    and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation raises
781	    exactly as that function does (and is screened before ``scenarios``).
782	    A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or a non-integer
783	    weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
784	    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight
785	    raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness,
786	    generates no keys and changes no state, and repeated calls with the
787	    same inputs return item-for-item identical results.
788	    """
789	    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
790	    validated_scenarios = _validate_scheme_weight_scenarios(scenarios)
791	
792	    metric_rows = tuple(
793	        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
794	    )
795	    spans = tuple(
796	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
797	        for i in range(2)
798	    )
799	
800	    def normalised(row: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction]:
801	        return tuple(
802	            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
803	            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
804	        )
805	
806	    normalised_rows = tuple(normalised(row) for row in metric_rows)
807	    scenario_totals = tuple(sum(weights) for weights in validated_scenarios)
808	
809	    def scenario_scores(row: tuple[Fraction, Fraction]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
810	        return tuple(
811	            sum(
812	                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, row)),
813	                Fraction(0),
814	            )
815	            / weight_total
816	            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
817	        )
818	
819	    score_rows = tuple(scenario_scores(row) for row in normalised_rows)
820	    scenario_best = tuple(
821	        min(row[scenario_index] for row in score_rows)
822	        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
823	    )
824	
825	    def ranking(entry: tuple[Params, tuple[Fraction, ...]]) -> tuple:
826	        candidate, scores = entry
827	        regrets = tuple(
828	            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)
829	        )
830	        return (
831	            max(regrets),
832	            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),
833	            scores,
834	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
835	            candidate.scheme,
836	            candidate.w is not None,
837	            candidate.w,
838	            candidate.height is not None,
839	            candidate.height,
840	        )
841	
842	    return min(zip(frontier, score_rows), key=ranking)[0]

845	@dataclass(frozen=True)
846	class SchemeScore:
847	    """Frozen decision-cost breakdown for one cross-scheme configuration.
848	
849	    One row of :func:`explain_scheme_weighted`'s result. Fields, in
850	    positional order:
851	
852	    - ``params``: the candidate's :class:`Params` static metrics;
853	    - ``signature_cost`` / ``steps_cost``: the candidate's two
854	      min-max-normalised costs, in the same order as the weights — one
855	      signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the
856	      verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`) — each
857	      ``(x - min) / (max - min)`` over the whole frontier, with a zero
858	      span scoring ``0``;
859	    - ``score``: the final weighted score — the two normalised costs
860	      times their weights, summed and divided by the weight total;
861	    - ``selected``: ``True`` on exactly the one row
862	      :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted` would pick.
863	
864	    Every normalised cost and the score is an exact
865	    :class:`fractions.Fraction`. Instances are frozen, support positional
866	    construction and compare (and hash) by value; no key material or
867	    randomness is involved.
868	    """
869	
870	    params: Params
871	    signature_cost: Fraction
872	    steps_cost: Fraction
873	    score: Fraction
874	    selected: bool
875	
876	
877	def explain_scheme_weighted(
878	    capacity: Any,
879	    budgets: Any,
880	    weights: Any,
881	) -> tuple[SchemeScore, ...]:
882	    """Export the decision-cost breakdown of the weighted scheme ranking.
883	
884	    The explanatory counterpart of :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted`: it
885	    computes :func:`scheme_frontier` exactly once and, instead of
886	    returning only the winning configuration, returns one frozen
887	    :class:`SchemeScore` row per frontier member, in the frontier's own
888	    order. Each row carries the candidate's :class:`Params` static
889	    metrics, its two min-max-normalised costs in the same order as the
890	    weights — one signature's serialised size
891	    (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier hash-chain step count
892	    (:attr:`Params.steps`) — the final weighted score and a ``selected``
893	    flag.
894	
895	    ``weights`` must be a two-tuple in that same order — single-signature
896	    serialised size and verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a
897	    non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least one must be positive.
898	    Each of the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier
899	    as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``; the
900	    score is the sum of the two normalised costs times their weights,
901	    divided by the weight total, all exact rationals
902	    (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point anywhere. Exactly
903	    one row is selected: the one whose :class:`Params`
904	    :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted` returns for the same arguments,
905	    field for field — the smallest score, with equal scores broken
906	    ascending by spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the requested
907	    signature count), scheme name, then ``w`` and ``height``, a missing
908	    parameter sorting ahead of any value. Lighting just one dimension
909	    selects that dimension's minimum; when every span is zero every row
910	    scores ``0`` and the tie-break tail alone decides, which the rows
911	    report exactly.
912	
913	    ``capacity`` and the two-tuple ``budgets`` follow
914	    :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget, exception
915	    and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation raises
916	    exactly as that function does (and is screened before ``weights``).
917	    A non-tuple ``weights`` container or a non-integer member raises
918	    ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a boolean, negative or
919	    all-zero weight raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
920	    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
921	    """
922	    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
923	    validated_weights = _validate_scheme_weights(weights)
924	
925	    metric_rows = tuple(
926	        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
927	    )
928	    spans = tuple(
929	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
930	        for i in range(2)
931	    )
932	    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)
933	
934	    entries = []
935	    for candidate, row in zip(frontier, metric_rows):
936	        costs = tuple(
937	            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
938	            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
939	        )
940	        score = sum(
941	            (weight * cost for weight, cost in zip(validated_weights, costs)),
942	            Fraction(0),
943	        ) / weight_total
944	        entries.append((candidate, costs, score))
945	
946	    def ranking(
947	        entry: tuple[Params, tuple[Fraction, ...], Fraction],
948	    ) -> tuple:
949	        candidate, _costs, entry_score = entry
950	        return (
951	            entry_score,
952	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
953	            candidate.scheme,
954	            candidate.w is not None,
955	            candidate.w,
956	            candidate.height is not None,
957	            candidate.height,
958	        )
959	
960	    chosen = min(entries, key=ranking)[0]
961	    return tuple(
962	        SchemeScore(candidate, *costs, score, candidate is chosen)
963	        for candidate, costs, score in entries
964	    )

967	def recommend_merkle_deployment(
968	    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
969	) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
970	    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.
971	
972	    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
973	    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
974	    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
975	    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.
976	
977	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
978	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
979	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire

981	    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)

def _scheme_candidates(capacity: int) -> list[Params]:
    """Enumerate every profile() configuration covering ``capacity``."""
    candidates: list[Params] = []
    if capacity == 1:
        candidates.append(profile("lamport"))
        for w in (4, 8):
            candidates.append(profile("wots", w=w))
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            candidate = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)
            if candidate.capacity >= capacity:
                candidates.append(candidate)
    return candidates


def recommend_scheme(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the :class:`Params` of the scheme best fitting capacity/budgets.

    The cross-scheme counterpart of :func:`recommend`: instead of choosing
    only among Merkle configurations, enumerate every configuration
    :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS
    with ``w`` 4 and 8) and every Merkle configuration with ``w`` in
    ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — keep those whose ``capacity``
    covers the requested signature count and that satisfy both budgets, and
    rank the feasible set. The one-time candidates cover one signature and
    are present only when ``capacity == 1``; a request for more than one
    signature leaves the Merkle configurations as the only candidates.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
    signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and on the
    verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`). Each entry is
    either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at
    least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` (the default) ranks candidates by ``sig_bytes`` first
    and ``steps`` second; ``prefer="speed"`` reverses the two. Both share
    the same ascending tie-break afterwards: spare capacity
    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), the scheme
    name lexicographically, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing
    parameter sorted ahead of any value. The first candidate after sorting
    is returned as a :class:`Params`.

    Validation runs capacity first, budgets second and ``prefer`` last. A
    non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a boolean, non-integer or
    out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal
    ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``), an unknown
    ``prefer`` value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises
    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
    no keys and changes no state.
    """
    capacity = _validate_scheme_capacity(capacity)
    signature_limit, steps_limit = _validate_scheme_budgets(budgets)
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')

    candidates = _scheme_candidates(capacity)

    feasible = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
            continue
        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
            continue
        feasible.append(candidate)
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
        tail = (
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (candidate.steps, candidate.sig_bytes) + tail
        return (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) + tail

    return min(feasible, key=ranking)


def scheme_frontier(capacity: Any, budgets: Any) -> tuple[Params, ...]:
    """Return every feasible, non-dominated scheme configuration as a tuple.

    The non-dominated-frontier counterpart of :func:`recommend_scheme`:
    instead of ranking the feasible configs and returning one preference's
    winner, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
    inspect the trade-off between one-signature size and verifier chain
    steps. The candidate set is exactly the one :func:`recommend_scheme`
    documents — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS with ``w`` 4
    and 8) at ``capacity == 1`` and every Merkle configuration with ``w``
    in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 whose capacity covers the
    requested count — and the capacity, one-signature serialised-size
    (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and verifier hash-chain step
    (:attr:`Params.steps`) metrics are field-for-field the values
    :func:`profile` reports.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
    signature's serialised size and on the verifier hash-chain step count.
    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
    integer, and at least one entry must be set; a candidate exceeding
    either bound is excluded. There is no preference parameter: no
    configuration trading chain steps for signature size (or the reverse)
    is discarded ahead of the dominance test, so both the speed and the
    size end of the trade-off survive.

    A feasible candidate *A* dominates another feasible candidate *B*
    when ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on both costs — signature bytes
    and verifier steps — and strictly smaller on at least one. Every
    dominated candidate is dropped and the survivors are deduplicated by
    value. The returned tuple is sorted stably and ascending by verifier
    steps, signature bytes, spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the
    requested count), scheme name, ``w`` and ``height``; a missing
    parameter sorts ahead of any value at its position.

    Validation reuses :func:`recommend_scheme`'s rules in its capacity-
    then-budgets order: a non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a
    boolean, non-integer or out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or
    otherwise illegal ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``)
    or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError`` — an
    empty tuple is never returned. The function is pure: it draws no
    randomness, generates no keys and changes no state, and repeated calls
    with the same inputs return item-for-item identical results.
    """
    capacity = _validate_scheme_capacity(capacity)
    signature_limit, steps_limit = _validate_scheme_budgets(budgets)

    feasible: list[Params] = []
    for candidate in _scheme_candidates(capacity):
        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
            continue
        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
            continue
        feasible.append(candidate)
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def dominates(a: Params, b: Params) -> bool:
        no_worse = a.sig_bytes <= b.sig_bytes and a.steps <= b.steps
        strictly_better = a.sig_bytes < b.sig_bytes or a.steps < b.steps
        return no_worse and strictly_better

    non_dominated = [
        candidate
        for candidate in feasible
        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in feasible)
    ]

    unique: list[Params] = []
    seen: set[Params] = set()
    for candidate in non_dominated:
        if candidate not in seen:
            seen.add(candidate)
            unique.append(candidate)

    unique.sort(
        key=lambda candidate: (
            candidate.steps,
            candidate.sig_bytes,
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )
    )
    return tuple(unique)


def _validate_scheme_weights(weights: Any) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Validate the two-tuple of non-negative scheme cost weights."""
    if not isinstance(weights, tuple):
        raise TypeError("weights must be a 2-tuple of non-negative integer weights")
    if len(weights) != 2:
        raise ValueError("weights must contain exactly two entries")
    for weight in weights:
        if isinstance(weight, bool):
            raise ValueError("every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
        if not isinstance(weight, int):
            raise TypeError("every weight must be an integer")
        if weight < 0:
            raise ValueError("every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
    if not any(weight > 0 for weight in weights):
        raise ValueError("at least one weight must be positive")
    return weights


def recommend_scheme_weighted(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, weights: Any) -> Params:
    """Pick one non-dominated scheme configuration by weighted normalised costs.

    Computes :func:`scheme_frontier` exactly once and ranks the returned
    feasible, non-dominated cross-scheme configurations by a
    caller-supplied linear score over two costs: one signature's
    serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier
    hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`).

    ``weights`` must be a two-tuple in that same order — single-signature
    serialised size and verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a
    non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least one must be positive.
    Each of the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier
    as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``; the
    weighted score is the sum of the two normalised costs times their
    weights, divided by the weight total, all compared as exact rationals
    (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point anywhere. The survivor
    with the smallest score is returned; equal scores use
    :func:`recommend_scheme`'s existing tie-break tail: spare capacity
    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), scheme name,
    then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing parameter sorted ahead of any
    value. The candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
    duplicated: the frontier is the only source of candidates and is
    called exactly once, so the returned :class:`Params` is field-for-field
    a member of the tuple one same-argument :func:`scheme_frontier` call
    returns.

    ``capacity`` and ``budgets`` follow :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types,
    ranges, inclusive-budget, exception and no-feasible-candidate rules
    exactly, so a violation raises exactly as that function does (and is
    screened before ``weights``). A non-tuple ``weights`` or a
    non-integer member raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a
    boolean, negative or all-zero weight raises ``ValueError``. The
    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and
    changes no state.
    """
    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
    validated_weights = _validate_scheme_weights(weights)

    metric_rows = tuple(
        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
    )
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(2)
    )
    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)

    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
        score = Fraction(0)
        for value, weight, (low, high) in zip(
            (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps), validated_weights, spans
        ):
            if high > low:
                score += weight * Fraction(value - low, high - low)
        score /= weight_total
        return (
            score,
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )

    return min(frontier, key=ranking)


def _validate_scheme_weight_scenarios(
    scenarios: Any,
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]:
    """Validate the non-empty tuple of two-weight scenarios."""
    if not isinstance(scenarios, tuple):
        raise TypeError("scenarios must be a tuple of two-tuples of weights")
    if not scenarios:
        raise ValueError("scenarios must not be empty")
    validated = []
    for scenario in scenarios:
        if not isinstance(scenario, tuple):
            raise TypeError("every scenario must be a two-tuple of weights")
        if len(scenario) != 2:
            raise ValueError("every scenario must contain exactly two entries")
        for weight in scenario:
            if isinstance(weight, bool):
                raise ValueError(
                    "every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer"
                )
            if not isinstance(weight, int):
                raise TypeError("every weight must be an integer")
            if weight < 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    "every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer"
                )
        if not any(weight > 0 for weight in scenario):
            raise ValueError(
                "every scenario must contain at least one positive weight"
            )
        validated.append(scenario)
    return tuple(validated)


def recommend_scheme_weighted_scenarios(
    capacity: Any,
    budgets: Any,
    scenarios: Any,
) -> Params:
    """Pick one non-dominated scheme minimising worst regret over scenarios.

    The preference-drift-robust counterpart of
    :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted`: instead of trusting one fixed
    two-tuple of cost weights, it evaluates several weight scenarios at
    once and picks the member of :func:`scheme_frontier`'s returned
    feasible, non-dominated cross-scheme frontier with the smallest
    worst-case regret — the maximum, over scenarios, of how much worse
    the chosen configuration scores than the best configuration for that
    scenario. The two weighted costs, in order, are one signature's
    serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier
    hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`).

    ``scenarios`` must be a non-empty tuple; each member must itself be a
    two-tuple in that same order — single-signature serialised size and
    verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a non-boolean,
    non-negative integer and at least one weight of each scenario must be
    positive; repeated scenarios are counted separately.

    The frontier is computed exactly once and is the only source of
    candidates — the candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
    duplicated, no randomness is drawn and no keys are generated. Each of
    the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier as
    ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``. For each
    scenario, a candidate's score is the weighted sum of its two
    normalised costs divided by the scenario's weight total, all compared
    as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point
    anywhere. Each scenario's own minimum score is then subtracted from
    every candidate's score to give that scenario's regret; candidates
    are ranked first by the greatest regret over the scenarios (the
    minimax-regret choice), then by the sum of the regrets, then by the
    tuple of per-scenario scores, all ascending. Every ranking finishes
    with the same ascending tie-break as every other cross-scheme
    ranking — spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the requested
    signature count), scheme name, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a
    missing parameter sorted ahead of any value — and the first survivor
    is returned as a :class:`Params`, field-for-field a member of the
    tuple one same-argument :func:`scheme_frontier` call returns.

    ``capacity`` and the two-tuple ``budgets`` follow
    :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget, exception
    and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation raises
    exactly as that function does (and is screened before ``scenarios``).
    A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or a non-integer
    weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight
    raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness,
    generates no keys and changes no state, and repeated calls with the
    same inputs return item-for-item identical results.
    """
    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
    validated_scenarios = _validate_scheme_weight_scenarios(scenarios)

    metric_rows = tuple(
        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
    )
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(2)
    )

    def normalised(row: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction]:
        return tuple(
            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
        )

    normalised_rows = tuple(normalised(row) for row in metric_rows)
    scenario_totals = tuple(sum(weights) for weights in validated_scenarios)

    def scenario_scores(row: tuple[Fraction, Fraction]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
        return tuple(
            sum(
                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, row)),
                Fraction(0),
            )
            / weight_total
            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
        )

    score_rows = tuple(scenario_scores(row) for row in normalised_rows)
    scenario_best = tuple(
        min(row[scenario_index] for row in score_rows)
        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
    )

    def ranking(entry: tuple[Params, tuple[Fraction, ...]]) -> tuple:
        candidate, scores = entry
        regrets = tuple(
            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)
        )
        return (
            max(regrets),
            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),
            scores,
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )

    return min(zip(frontier, score_rows), key=ranking)[0]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SchemeScore:
    """Frozen decision-cost breakdown for one cross-scheme configuration.

    One row of :func:`explain_scheme_weighted`'s result. Fields, in
    positional order:

    - ``params``: the candidate's :class:`Params` static metrics;
    - ``signature_cost`` / ``steps_cost``: the candidate's two
      min-max-normalised costs, in the same order as the weights — one
      signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the
      verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`) — each
      ``(x - min) / (max - min)`` over the whole frontier, with a zero
      span scoring ``0``;
    - ``score``: the final weighted score — the two normalised costs
      times their weights, summed and divided by the weight total;
    - ``selected``: ``True`` on exactly the one row
      :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted` would pick.

    Every normalised cost and the score is an exact
    :class:`fractions.Fraction`. Instances are frozen, support positional
    construction and compare (and hash) by value; no key material or
    randomness is involved.
    """

    params: Params
    signature_cost: Fraction
    steps_cost: Fraction
    score: Fraction
    selected: bool


def explain_scheme_weighted(
    capacity: Any,
    budgets: Any,
    weights: Any,
) -> tuple[SchemeScore, ...]:
    """Export the decision-cost breakdown of the weighted scheme ranking.

    The explanatory counterpart of :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted`: it
    computes :func:`scheme_frontier` exactly once and, instead of
    returning only the winning configuration, returns one frozen
    :class:`SchemeScore` row per frontier member, in the frontier's own
    order. Each row carries the candidate's :class:`Params` static
    metrics, its two min-max-normalised costs in the same order as the
    weights — one signature's serialised size
    (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and the verifier hash-chain step count
    (:attr:`Params.steps`) — the final weighted score and a ``selected``
    flag.

    ``weights`` must be a two-tuple in that same order — single-signature
    serialised size and verifier chain steps. Every weight must be a
    non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least one must be positive.
    Each of the two costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier
    as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``; the
    score is the sum of the two normalised costs times their weights,
    divided by the weight total, all exact rationals
    (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point anywhere. Exactly
    one row is selected: the one whose :class:`Params`
    :func:`recommend_scheme_weighted` returns for the same arguments,
    field for field — the smallest score, with equal scores broken
    ascending by spare capacity (candidate capacity minus the requested
    signature count), scheme name, then ``w`` and ``height``, a missing
    parameter sorting ahead of any value. Lighting just one dimension
    selects that dimension's minimum; when every span is zero every row
    scores ``0`` and the tie-break tail alone decides, which the rows
    report exactly.

    ``capacity`` and the two-tuple ``budgets`` follow
    :func:`scheme_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget, exception
    and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation raises
    exactly as that function does (and is screened before ``weights``).
    A non-tuple ``weights`` container or a non-integer member raises
    ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a boolean, negative or
    all-zero weight raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
    """
    frontier = scheme_frontier(capacity, budgets)
    validated_weights = _validate_scheme_weights(weights)

    metric_rows = tuple(
        (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) for candidate in frontier
    )
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(2)
    )
    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)

    entries = []
    for candidate, row in zip(frontier, metric_rows):
        costs = tuple(
            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
        )
        score = sum(
            (weight * cost for weight, cost in zip(validated_weights, costs)),
            Fraction(0),
        ) / weight_total
        entries.append((candidate, costs, score))

    def ranking(
        entry: tuple[Params, tuple[Fraction, ...], Fraction],
    ) -> tuple:
        candidate, _costs, entry_score = entry
        return (
            entry_score,
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )

    chosen = min(entries, key=ranking)[0]
    return tuple(
        SchemeScore(candidate, *costs, score, candidate is chosen)
        for candidate, costs, score in entries
    )


def recommend_merkle_deployment(
    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.

    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``

    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.

    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.

    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
    no state.
    """
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")

      checkpoint bytes, any single group's transport peak, aggregate
      transport bytes, per-signature verifier chain steps and carried
      multi-proof nodes — each ``(x - min) / (max - min)`` over the whole
      frontier, with a zero span scoring ``0``;
    - ``scores``: the per-scenario weighted scores, in the same order as
      the input scenarios — each the five normalised costs times that

    - ``regrets``: the per-scenario regrets, in the same order — each

    - ``selected``: ``True`` on exactly the one row

    Every normalised cost, score and regret is an exact
    :class:`fractions.Fraction`. Instances are frozen, support positional
    construction and compare (and hash) by value; no key material or
    randomness is involved.
    """

    workload: MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile
    checkpoint_cost: Fraction
    peak_cost: Fraction

def explain_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios(
    capacity: Any,
    groups: Any,
    budgets: Any,
    scenarios: Any,
) -> tuple[MerkleModeScenarioScore, ...]:
    """Export the multi-scenario breakdown of the weighted mode ranking.

    The explanatory counterpart of
    :func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios`: it computes
    :func:`merkle_mode_frontier` exactly once and, instead of returning
    only the winning plan, returns one frozen
    :class:`MerkleModeScenarioScore` row per frontier member, in the
    frontier's own order. Each row carries the candidate's
    :class:`MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile` mode plan, its five
    min-max-normalised costs in the same order as the weights — the
    checkpoint bytes (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), any
    single group's transport peak (the maximum of
    :attr:`MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile.sizes`), the aggregate transport
    bytes (:attr:`MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile.total`), the
    per-signature verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle",
    ...)``'s ``steps``) and the total carried multi-proof node count,
    using the mode frontier's definition: it accumulates the canonical
    node count of every group carried as a multi-proof and counts ``0``
    for every group carried as a batch proof — the per-scenario weighted
    scores, the per-scenario regrets and a ``selected`` flag.

    ``scenarios`` must be a non-empty tuple; each member must itself be a
    five-tuple in that same order — checkpoint bytes, single-group peak,
    total transport bytes, per-signature chain steps and carried nodes.
    Every weight must be a non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least
    one weight of each scenario must be positive; repeated scenarios are
    counted separately, exactly like repeated groups. Each of the five
    costs is min-max normalised over the whole frontier as
    ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span scoring ``0``. For each
    scenario, a candidate's score is the weighted sum of its five
    normalised costs divided by the scenario's weight total, and its
    regret is that score minus the scenario's best score over the whole
    frontier — all exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no
    floating point anywhere. Exactly one row is selected: the one whose
    plan :func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios` returns for the
    same arguments, field for field — the smallest worst regret, with
    ties broken by the regret sum, then the per-scenario score tuple,
    then ascending by checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w``, ``height`` and
    the ``modes`` tuple in lexicographic order.

    ``capacity``, ``groups`` and the five-tuple ``budgets`` follow
    :func:`merkle_mode_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget,
    exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation
    raises exactly as that function does (and is screened before
    ``scenarios``). A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or a
    non-integer weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight
    raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness,
    generates no keys and changes no state.
    """
    frontier = merkle_mode_frontier(capacity, groups, budgets)
    validated_scenarios = _validate_weight_scenarios(scenarios)

    def metrics(
        workload: MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile,
    ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
        nodes = sum(
            merkle_transport_profile(
                workload.config.w, workload.config.height, group
            )[0]
            for mode, group in zip(workload.modes, groups)
            if mode == "multiproof"
        )
        return (
            workload.config.checkpoint_bytes,
            max(workload.sizes),
            workload.total,
            profile(
                "merkle", w=workload.config.w, height=workload.config.height
            ).steps,
            nodes,
        )

    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(workload) for workload in frontier)
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(5)
    )
    scenario_totals = tuple(sum(weights) for weights in validated_scenarios)

    entries = []
    for workload, row in zip(frontier, metric_rows):
        costs = tuple(
            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
        )
        scores = tuple(
            sum(
                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, costs)),
                Fraction(0),
            )
            / weight_total
            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
        )
        entries.append((workload, costs, scores))

    scenario_best = tuple(
        min(entry[2][scenario_index] for entry in entries)
        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
    )
    entries = [
        (workload, costs, scores, tuple(
            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)
        ))
        for workload, costs, scores in entries
    ]

    def ranking(
        entry: tuple[
            MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile,
            tuple[Fraction, ...],
            tuple[Fraction, ...],
            tuple[Fraction, ...],
        ],
    ) -> tuple[
        Fraction,
        Fraction,
        tuple[Fraction, ...],
        int,
        int,
        int,
        int,
        tuple[str, ...],
    ]:
        workload, _costs, scores, regrets = entry
        config = workload.config
        return (
            max(regrets),
            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),
            scores,
            config.checkpoint_bytes,
            config.leaf_count,
            config.w,
            config.height,
            workload.modes,
        )

    chosen = min(entries, key=ranking)[0]
    return tuple(
        MerkleModeScenarioScore(
            workload, *costs, scores, regrets, workload is chosen
        )
        for workload, costs, scores, regrets in entries
    )


def _validate_verify_mode_budgets(budgets: Any) -> tuple[int | None, ...]:
    """Validate the six-tuple of verify-mode-frontier budget limits."""
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 6-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 6:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly six entries")
    labels = ("checkpoint", "group", "total", "steps", "nodes", "hashes")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    return tuple(limits)

180	sign_ots_pair signs one message with a Lamport/W-OTS signer pair under a
181	joint lock and returns both signatures together with the v2 envelopes of
182	the two advanced states, so the pair either advances together or not at
183	all; sign_with_checkpoint on each one-time signer and
184	sign_ots_pair_with_checkpoint for the pair are the plaintext atomic
185	counterparts, returning the signature(s) together with the raw v1
186	checkpoint bytes of the advanced state(s) in one locked step;
187	sign_ots_pair_proof_with_checkpoint is its proof-packing counterpart,
188	returning the OtsPairProof of the two fresh signatures together with the
189	two raw v1 checkpoint bytes in one locked step;
190	sign_ots_pair_proof_with_auth_state is the authenticated counterpart of
191	that proof-packing entry, returning the same OtsPairProof together with
192	the two v2 auth_state_wrap envelopes of the advanced states (Lamport
193	first, W-OTS second) in one locked step;
194	sign_ots_pair_proof_auth_state is the stateless conversion entry: it
195	authenticates a same-generation Lamport/W-OTS v2 envelope pair (both tags
196	constant-time first), restores their v1 checkpoints, signs one message
197	with each throwaway signer, and returns the OtsPairProof, the two
198	next-generation envelopes (Lamport first, W-OTS second) and g+1, all
199	under one paired claim over the (g, g+1) transition that runs only after
200	every output exists and keeps no hidden state;
201	sign_lamport_auth_state and sign_wots_auth_state are the single-signer
202	stateless restore-sign-wrap conversions for the two one-time schemes: each
203	authenticates the matching v2 envelope, restores its v1 checkpoint, signs
204	one message with the throwaway signer, and returns the signature, the
205	next-generation envelope of the used state and g+1 under one paired
206	(("scheme", g), ("scheme", g+1)) claim that runs only after every output
207	exists and keeps no hidden state;
208	restore_merkle_claimed does the same one-step authenticated restore and
209	claim for a Merkle signer v2 envelope; restore_lattice_claimed does it
210	for a toy lattice private key v2 envelope, restoring the key with
211	ToyLatticePrivateKey.from_bytes and claiming ("lattice", generation).
212	sign_merkle_auth_state is the stateless restore-sign-wrap conversion: it
213	authenticates a Merkle v2 envelope and restores its v1 payload, signs the
214	restored signer's current minimum leaf, wraps the advanced checkpoint at
215	generation g+1 and, only once every output exists, performs one paired
216	claim over the (g, g+1) transition — it keeps no hidden state and changes
217	no old interface or wire byte. sign_merkle_auth_state_batch is the batch
218	counterpart: it restores the same way, signs a non-empty tuple of messages
219	with consecutive leaves in a single sign_batch run, and returns the
220	signature tuple together with the envelope and generation g+1.
221	sign_multiproof_merkle_auth_state is its multiproof counterpart: it
222	restores the same way, signs the batch on consecutive leaves from the
223	current index (or on an explicit strictly increasing indices selection,
224	voiding the gaps), and returns the deduplicated multiproof_encode proof
225	bytes over the batch together with the envelope and generation g+1.
226	advance_merkle_auth_state is the stateless authenticated counterpart of
227	MerkleSigner.advance_to_with_auth_state: it restores the same way, advances
228	the next-leaf index with advance_to semantics (an equal target is legal and
229	still yields the next-generation envelope), and returns the (before, after)
230	index pair together with the envelope and generation g+1, all under one
231	(g, g+1) claim that runs only after every output exists.
232	advance_and_sign_merkle_auth_state combines the two: it restores the same
233	way, advances the next-leaf index to a caller-chosen target (the leaf count
234	itself is not legal — the target leaf must remain signable), signs one
235	message with that target leaf, and returns the (before, target) index pair,
236	the signature, the envelope and generation g+1, again under a single
237	(g, g+1) claim that runs only after every output exists.
238	advance_and_sign_merkle_auth_state_batch is its batch counterpart: it
239	restores the same way, advances to a caller-chosen still-signable target and
240	then signs a non-empty tuple of messages on the consecutive leaves from
241	that target in a single sign_batch run, returning the (before, target)
242	index pair, the signature tuple, the envelope and generation g+1, all under
243	the same single (g, g+1) claim.
244	advance_and_multiproof_merkle_auth_state is its multiproof counterpart: it
245	restores and advances the same way, signs the same consecutive batch from
246	the target, and returns the (before, target) index pair, the deduplicated
247	multiproof_encode proof bytes over the batch, the envelope and generation
248	g+1, again under the same single (g, g+1) claim.
249	Both envelopes authenticate but do not encrypt and give no replay
250	protection on their own.

531	def _validate_bits(bits: Any) -> int:
532	    if isinstance(bits, bool) or not isinstance(bits, int) or not 1 <= bits <= BITS:
533	        raise ValueError(f"bits must be a non-boolean integer between 1 and {BITS}")
534	    return bits
535

537	def _validate_container(elements: Any, label: str) -> None:
538	    if not isinstance(elements, tuple):
539	        raise TypeError(f"{label} collection must be a tuple of {HASH_BYTES}-byte values")
540	    for element in elements:
541	        if not isinstance(element, bytes):
542	            raise TypeError(f"every {label} must be bytes")
543	        if len(element) != HASH_BYTES:
544	            raise ValueError(f"every {label} must be exactly {HASH_BYTES} bytes")

547	def _encode_v1(magic: bytes, bits: int, elements: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> bytes:
548	    """Shared v1 layout: magic, version, ``bits``, element count, elements."""
549	    return (
550	        magic
551	        + bytes((_CODEC_VERSION,))
552	        + bits.to_bytes(2, "big")
553	        + len(elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
554	        + b"".join(elements)
555	    )

558	def _decode_v1(data: Any, magic: bytes, name: str, *, is_key: bool) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
559	    """Parse a v1 blob into ``(bits, elements)``; ``name`` labels errors.
560	
561	    Keys carry ``2 * bits`` elements, signatures carry ``bits``.
562	    """

"""pqattest - hash-based one-time and few-times signatures, plus a toy KEM.

Public API: keygen / public_key_from / sign / verify / message_bits /
OneTimeSigner / KeyExhaustedError, with a deterministic, versioned v1 binary
codec for the Lamport keys and stateless signatures:
PrivateKey.to_bytes / PrivateKey.from_bytes,
PublicKey.to_bytes / PublicKey.from_bytes,
lamport_signature_to_bytes / lamport_signature_from_bytes, and a versioned
state checkpoint for the signer: OneTimeSigner.checkpoint /
OneTimeSigner.from_checkpoint; the Winternitz
construction: wots_keygen / wots_sign / wots_verify / WOTSPrivateKey /
WOTSPublicKey / WOTSOneTimeSigner / wots_signature_to_bytes /
wots_signature_from_bytes, plus the standalone one-time proof packs
LamportProof and WOTSProof that bundle each construction's public key and
signature into one independently transportable, deterministic v1 byte
block, and OtsPairProof that pairs one LamportProof with one WOTSProof
for the same message into a single independently transportable v1 byte
block (its verify_bound additionally binds the pair to the receiver's
expected public keys), Merkle-aggregated W-OTS: MerkleSigner /
MerklePublicKey / MerkleSignature / MerkleProof / MerkleBatchProof /
merkle_verify / multiproof_encode / multiproof_verify /
multiproof_verify_bound (the two proof classes' verify_bound and this

parameter analysis: Params / profile / recommend / recommend_scheme /

recommend_scheme_weighted to rank that cross-scheme frontier by a

verify-mode frontier by one of five business preferences (compact /
verify / nodes / speed / robust),
recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment_weighted to rank that same
fixed-position verify-mode frontier by a five-tuple of non-negative weights
over min-max-normalised costs (total transport, single-group peak, total
verifier hashes, carried nodes and per-signature chain steps), the weighted
sum divided by the weight total, with exact Fraction arithmetic,
explain_merkle_verify_mode_deployment_weighted to export that same weighted
fixed-position ranking's decision-cost breakdown as a tuple of frozen
MerkleVerifyModeDeploymentScore rows — one per frontier member, in frontier
order, each carrying the candidate's plan/cost pairing, its five
normalised costs, its final score and a selected flag — again with exact
Fraction arithmetic,
and
the teaching-only toy lattice KEM: toy_lattice_keygen / toy_lattice_encapsulate /
toy_lattice_decapsulate / ToyLatticePublicKey / ToyLatticePrivateKey /
ToyLatticeCiphertext. The three plaintext signer checkpoints and the toy
lattice private key's versioned encoding can be sealed
in a keyed HMAC-SHA-256 envelope with auth_wrap / auth_unwrap; a v2
envelope with auth_state_wrap / auth_state_unwrap additionally binds a
uint64 generation so an externally tracked floor can detect rollback.
The Lamport and W-OTS signers additionally offer from_auth_state, which
authenticates and restores a v2 envelope and then invokes a caller-supplied
monotonic claim callback exactly once; restore_ots_pair restores a
same-generation Lamport/W-OTS pair and claims both sides with a single
callback, so a claim can never succeed for only one side;
sign_ots_pair signs one message with a Lamport/W-OTS signer pair under a
joint lock and returns both signatures together with the v2 envelopes of
the two advanced states, so the pair either advances together or not at
all; sign_with_checkpoint on each one-time signer and
sign_ots_pair_with_checkpoint for the pair are the plaintext atomic
counterparts, returning the signature(s) together with the raw v1
checkpoint bytes of the advanced state(s) in one locked step;
sign_ots_pair_proof_with_checkpoint is its proof-packing counterpart,
returning the OtsPairProof of the two fresh signatures together with the
two raw v1 checkpoint bytes in one locked step;
sign_ots_pair_proof_with_auth_state is the authenticated counterpart of
that proof-packing entry, returning the same OtsPairProof together with
the two v2 auth_state_wrap envelopes of the advanced states (Lamport
first, W-OTS second) in one locked step;
sign_ots_pair_proof_auth_state is the stateless conversion entry: it
authenticates a same-generation Lamport/W-OTS v2 envelope pair (both tags
constant-time first), restores their v1 checkpoints, signs one message
with each throwaway signer, and returns the OtsPairProof, the two
next-generation envelopes (Lamport first, W-OTS second) and g+1, all
under one paired claim over the (g, g+1) transition that runs only after
every output exists and keeps no hidden state;
sign_lamport_auth_state and sign_wots_auth_state are the single-signer
stateless restore-sign-wrap conversions for the two one-time schemes: each
authenticates the matching v2 envelope, restores its v1 checkpoint, signs
one message with the throwaway signer, and returns the signature, the
next-generation envelope of the used state and g+1 under one paired
(("scheme", g), ("scheme", g+1)) claim that runs only after every output
exists and keeps no hidden state;
restore_merkle_claimed does the same one-step authenticated restore and
claim for a Merkle signer v2 envelope; restore_lattice_claimed does it
for a toy lattice private key v2 envelope, restoring the key with
ToyLatticePrivateKey.from_bytes and claiming ("lattice", generation).
sign_merkle_auth_state is the stateless restore-sign-wrap conversion: it
authenticates a Merkle v2 envelope and restores its v1 payload, signs the
restored signer's current minimum leaf, wraps the advanced checkpoint at
generation g+1 and, only once every output exists, performs one paired
claim over the (g, g+1) transition — it keeps no hidden state and changes
no old interface or wire byte. sign_merkle_auth_state_batch is the batch
counterpart: it restores the same way, signs a non-empty tuple of messages
with consecutive leaves in a single sign_batch run, and returns the
signature tuple together with the envelope and generation g+1.
sign_multiproof_merkle_auth_state is its multiproof counterpart: it
restores the same way, signs the batch on consecutive leaves from the
current index (or on an explicit strictly increasing indices selection,
voiding the gaps), and returns the deduplicated multiproof_encode proof
bytes over the batch together with the envelope and generation g+1.
advance_merkle_auth_state is the stateless authenticated counterpart of
MerkleSigner.advance_to_with_auth_state: it restores the same way, advances
the next-leaf index with advance_to semantics (an equal target is legal and
still yields the next-generation envelope), and returns the (before, after)
index pair together with the envelope and generation g+1, all under one
(g, g+1) claim that runs only after every output exists.
advance_and_sign_merkle_auth_state combines the two: it restores the same
way, advances the next-leaf index to a caller-chosen target (the leaf count
itself is not legal — the target leaf must remain signable), signs one
message with that target leaf, and returns the (before, target) index pair,
the signature, the envelope and generation g+1, again under a single
(g, g+1) claim that runs only after every output exists.
advance_and_sign_merkle_auth_state_batch is its batch counterpart: it
restores the same way, advances to a caller-chosen still-signable target and
then signs a non-empty tuple of messages on the consecutive leaves from
that target in a single sign_batch run, returning the (before, target)
index pair, the signature tuple, the envelope and generation g+1, all under
the same single (g, g+1) claim.
advance_and_multiproof_merkle_auth_state is its multiproof counterpart: it
restores and advances the same way, signs the same consecutive batch from
the target, and returns the (before, target) index pair, the deduplicated
multiproof_encode proof bytes over the batch, the envelope and generation
g+1, again under the same single (g, g+1) claim.
Both envelopes authenticate but do not encrypt and give no replay
protection on their own.
"""
